# Fermionic Reset Complexity

Scientific repository <https://github.com/GoGoKo699/Fermionic-Reset-Complexity>

The task is reference-stable reset of an entire fermionic register with all modes retained. Both control classes use one unmonitored Markovian vacuum-loss port and charge its total integrated rate in every branch. Gaussian control is quadratic, including pairing. Interacting control can apply arbitrary fast even unitaries. Both classes may use input-independent Gaussian randomization whose record is discarded. No supplied pure quantum ancillary modes, feedback, measurements, or postselection enter the resource model.

At action cap A, the exact Gaussian half-diamond reset error is 1 - (1 - exp(-A/n)/2)^n + 2^(-n) exp(-A). The interacting action is Theta(n + ln(1/epsilon)) uniformly for n >= 2 and 0 < epsilon <= 1/2. At fixed n >= 2 the sharp error decay exponents in A are 1/n for Gaussian control and 1/2 for interacting control. At each fixed target error in the stated joint domain, the mirrored-tree construction attains leading linear coefficient at most 5/2 as n grows.

- Balanced single-port matchings, finite mirrored-tree sweeps, the odd no-jump determinant converse, sharp fixed-size precision exponent, and the finite three-mode separation. See science/interacting-frontier.md.
- Earlier reference-aware entropy compression, spectral inflow bound, and quantitative compression schedule. See science/interacting_reset.md and science/finite_size.md.

- Learning route. See learning/MILESTONES.md for exactly 30 project-defined understanding targets, earlier dependencies, conceptual connections, and source pointers.

## Keeping the two Gaussian optima distinct

The exact selected-input Gaussian vacuum population from I/2^n is (1 - exp(-A/n)/2)^n. For the universal task, the odd-parity input reduces that population by 2^(-n) exp(-A). The allowed parity twirl and vacuum dephasing attain the resulting worst-case error even with arbitrary reference correlations. In the interacting class the same state-to-channel reduction holds, while the finite-action interacting optimum for n >= 3 and the optimal large-register coefficient remain open.

The comparison concerns dissipative action. Coherent synthesis, locality, switching, and full hardware time are outside the action budget. The ordinary matrix-algebra half-diamond guarantee includes arbitrary reference systems. The learning map is independent of any reader's assessment history.
